### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**11** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-driven.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via FieldSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/field.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b005638268828ffdef8819f04b141a13296e7de4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c4977597e883eb2793c85d7073fdaa623b3c9dd0` — the merge of head `c6d372dcbee640d17b49375e50ea8951ea54c678` into base `b005638268828ffdef8819f04b141a13296e7de4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c4977597e883eb2793c85d7073fdaa623b3c9dd0 && git checkout c4977597e883eb2793c85d7073fdaa623b3c9dd0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b005638268828ffdef8819f04b141a13296e7de4 c6d372dcbee640d17b49375e50ea8951ea54c678 && git checkout -B drift-repro b005638268828ffdef8819f04b141a13296e7de4 && git merge --no-ff c6d372dcbee640d17b49375e50ea8951ea54c678

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b005638268828ffdef8819f04b141a13296e7de4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b005638268828ffdef8819f04b141a13296e7de4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c6d372dcbee640d17b49375e50ea8951ea54c678`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/record-currency-path.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.summary-dynamic-currency-rollup-home-amount-judged-as-served.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/record-currency-aggregate-door.ts, packages/objectql/src/protocol-batch-object-registration.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/record-currency-guards.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/currency-summary-home-rollup.test.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/data.json, packages/spec/export-origins/data.json, packages/spec/liveness/field.json

First contract review of PR #33855 for card #33713, on the schema face and the declared narrowing. Read: the diff per file against merge base `b76df9a6`, the card and its comments (claim 6893268160, amendment 6893463231, dev report 6894270946), the #33710 review (record ID: 6890873219), and, outside the diff and read only, `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (the single-save and run call sites of the follow door) and `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` (`refuseDishonestHomeAmount`). Prose faces (`.changeset`, `content/docs/**`) were read for agreement with the code and are the lane seat's to accept.

### ① Derived judgments

- The engine arm matches the stack pass. `followRefusalsOf` judges case (d) at the parent (its `dynamic` roll-ups over a registered child, or itself) and at the child (a registered parent's roll-up over a field this object holds). The predicate is the one `collectRecordCurrencyPathErrors` uses: a `summary` with `sum` / `min` / `max` / `avg` (`rawRollupOf`), a `currencyConfig` object whose mode is `dynamic` or absent, a child field the child holds, and `storedHomeAmountSourceOf` answering nothing. A child field the child does not hold is no verdict at either door. The stack pass still skips an end it knows only through an extension; the engine judges that end as served, which is the N6 half.
- One spelling. The case (d) sentence moved out of `stack.zod.ts` into `record-currency-path.ts` unchanged in its three arms; both doors call `recordCurrencyDynamicRollupNotHomeError`. The only wording difference from the old private copy is that the suggested home field and the candidate list now name valid home amounts only, which follows from N7.
- N7 matches the object door. `storedHomeAmountSourceOf` reads a `homeAmount` under the conditions `refuseDishonestHomeAmount` enforces on an authored object: declared on a `record`-mode `currency` amount, naming another field of the same map that is a `currency` field in `dynamic` (or absent) mode, `readonly: true`, no `expression`, and claimed by exactly one amount. An authored object that parses satisfies all of them, so `defineStack` answers as before for every stack whose fields are all authored; only a map merged with an extension, or an object as served, can now answer differently.
- N6 needed no new path. `registry.ts` is untouched; the single save, the batch writers and the end of a registration run already hand the follow door the object as served (`servedFoldWithLayer`), so an `extend` layer reaches the new arm by the existing route.
- Refusal code and status. Case (d) throws `RecordCurrencyFollowRefusedError`, the class the `record` case throws: `INVALID_METADATA`, 422. The metadata-API test asserts `status: 422`, `code: 'INVALID_METADATA'` and the class name for (d), and the same triple for the `record` control beside it.
- Ordering against D6 is unchanged: `recordCurrencySummaryRefusal` is asked before the follow door, so a roll-up over an amount in each row's own currency is still answered there, pinned by a test.
- Main drift. The branch is 19 commits behind `main`; none of them touches a file of this diff. One touches a sibling semantic entry file in the same directory, which does not collide.
- CI on this head at record time is not all green: see ③.

### ② Semver level

- Declared pair: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, identical in the PR body and the changeset. Both are right. The diff puts no new key or accepted value on a published payload, so the value is `no`; `yes (narrowing)` is the spelling for a diff that widens and narrows, and this one admits nothing that was refused before. A single save now refuses a body it stored on `main` and in a published `next` version, and `defineStack` refuses an extension-forged `homeAmount` it admitted, so the kind is `narrowed`.
- Level: the kind takes at least `minor` on each package whose `src` the diff moves. `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/objectql` are both `minor`. The changeset carries the `!`, the BREAKING banner, the FROM and TO lines and the one-line fix.
- ADR-0087: one marker, `registered summary-dynamic-currency-rollup-home-amount-judged-as-served`, and the entry file is new in the diff. See ④ for the shape ruling.
- Baselines: `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` gain exactly the two new exports of `record-currency-path.ts`; the two reference pages follow the one `describe` change; `liveness/field.json` gains a dated line and keeps the verdict LIVE.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: written through the relay.
- Independence: implemented and dispatched by `os-project-manager` (seat `domain:spec#4`); this account neither implemented nor dispatched it.
- No new id materialisation or in-app join: the arm reads field maps already in memory.
- No security boundary is moved. The refusal is display honesty (the stored total is right, the symbol could be wrong).
- CI: at 2026-11-15T12:58Z this head is NOT all green, and landing check ② is the lane seat's to clear. Every check run has completed: 56 succeeded, 10 were skipped and 2 are red, `Test Core (4/8)` and the `Test Core` roll-up that reports it. In the shard, one test of `packages/objectql/src/protocol-unmanaged-import-rename-battery.test.ts` (`names in step`), a file outside this diff, timed out at 5000 ms; the other 13150 tests of the package passed, the new describes among them. The same shard is green on merge base `b76df9a6` and on `main` `b0056382`, so the red does not carry the base's signature and is not waived by it. Nothing in the diff reads as its cause (the new arm adds one pass over an object's own fields per judged layer), but that is a reading, not a measurement: a re-run of the shard settles it, and a second red on the same test would be this PR's to answer. This verdict is on the contract and does not stand in for that check.

### ④ Design judgment

- `record-currency-path.ts`: holds. The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real at the door a running server meets; it takes no declared capability away. The shape `currencyMode: 'dynamic'` was admitted for in #33659, a roll-up of a stored home amount, saves and is served at both doors, in either registration order, for all four functions (controls in all three test files).
- `stack.zod.ts`: holds. The pass is unchanged in when it judges; it changes only in what counts as a home amount, and only for a field map the object door never parsed.
- `field.zod.ts`: holds. The `describe` sentence now names both doors, and both refuse.
- Ruling on the dev's open question (the ADR-0087 shape): A, keep the registered semantic entry. ADR-0087 as amended 2026-11-12 leaves a `narrowed` changeset two exits: a registered entry, or a category resting on a checked fact. None of the checked facts is true here, and the kind is right as declared, so the entry is the only truthful disposition. The measurement supports it on its own terms as well: a published `@objectstack/spec` version (`next`, 2026-11-15) accepts the body this door now refuses, and an author on it meets the refusal at the next save. That stable 18.4.0 never admitted the shape makes the entry narrow in audience, not wrong.
- Ruling on R7 at a single save: acceptable. A single save has judged its layer against an empty slot since #33621, for (a) and (c) alike, and `registry.ts` is not in this diff; (d) inherits the door it was asked to join. The consequence is bounded and recoverable: a pair stored under the `next` snapshot is refused at the next `/meta` save of either end, the message names the parent's roll-up and the fix, and saving the parent with the roll-up corrected clears it. A registration run compares the pair and does not refuse one it leaves as found, which is pinned; the cold boot is not asked.
- Tests hold against the claims: equality with `defineStack`'s finding at the engine door, both registration orders, the `{}` config, the de-homing child save, the run half of R7, N6 at a single save and at the end of a `registerApp` run, N7 forged and valid. Two ablations are reported with the reds they produced.

Finding S1 of the #33710 review (record ID: 6890873219) is answered by this diff as the card asked, with N1, N6 and N7 folded in.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Nits (accepted deviations, prose only, no effect on correctness or the contract):

- Nit a: the changeset and the entry's `surface` describe the child end as "a child saved so that a registered roll-up no longer reads a home amount". A single save compares against nothing, so an unchanged re-save of either end of a pair already stored is refused as well. The PR body says so; the upgrade text does not.
- Nit b: the entry's `reason` says such a roll-up "was stored" without saying that only the `next` snapshot admitted it; the changeset does say it.
- Nit c: the docblock above the single-save follow question in `registry.ts` still names only the following amount and the `record` roll-up. Outside the diff, noted by the dev.

Implemented-by: `session_01FEkQ5nU2dZbC2HWMg47r4D`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4cy7hQ5MvQ83ByNZ8ZH`

**VERDICT: PASS**
